# OSM map fixing, drawing-first and user-as-source-of-truth

The user is the source of truth: they know the road. Google Maps / Street View screenshots they send are only for understanding what they mean; never copy geometry, names or details from Google into OSM (terms forbid it). Only edit what the user confirms from their own local knowledge.

## 1. Understand the ask
- Get the location (address, intersection, or link) and what looks or feels wrong, or the behavior they see (e.g. 'FSD picks the wrong lane heading east', 'nav doesn't know about our gate').
- For FSD or routing complaints, ask where the trip starts and ends; lane choice often depends on upcoming turns, not tagging errors. Tesla is reported to use some OSM data but FSD's reliance on it isn't confirmed, so frame fixes as 'can help', never a guarantee.

## 2. Look up what OSM has (read-only)
- Geocode with Nominatim (set a User-Agent). Pull ways/nodes with Overpass (`out meta geom`; use a public mirror if overpass-api.de is unreachable) and edit history from api.openstreetmap.org.
- For each relevant way: id, highway, oneway, lanes, turn:lanes, placement, maxspeed, access, barrier nodes, last edit. Note where links join and on which side (compute from geometry).
- Optionally route the trip with the public OSRM demo to know which ways matter.

## 3. Draw it, often
- Make simple schematic PNGs (matplotlib): lanes as bands with lane lines, arrows per lane (through/turn), cross streets labeled, side links labeled with which side they join, distances, way ids with current tags along the bottom, big fonts. Title it 'What OSM has now'. Where OSM is silent (no lanes tag, no gate node), say so on the drawing.
- Send the drawing and ask one or two concrete questions ('Is the right lane straight-only?'). Prefer showing over describing. When the user's words are ambiguous, draw your best guess and let them confirm.
- After they answer, draw a two-row 'now vs proposed' diagram for any fix.
- If everything matches what they confirm, say so plainly: the map is fine and the behavior is likely the car's or app's own logic (suggest a Tesla voice bug report for FSD). Don't invent fixes.

## 4. Propose a minimal, wiki-compliant fix
- Check wiki.openstreetmap.org for current tagging; never invent tags. Use `note=` for details no tag covers.
- Keep scope to exactly what the user confirmed; ask before touching adjacent intersections or roads.
- Build an osmChange (.osc) from fresh API versions with negative ids for new elements; split ways rather than mis-tagging; don't add new nodes to unrelated shared outlines. Validate: XML parses, versions current, splits rejoin to original node lists, ways stay connected, no orphan nodes. Also write a readable before/after list.

## 5. Account and upload (only after explicit approval)
- Ask whether to sign up with the bot's own email inbox or the user's personal email, and which public display name to use. Sign up in the browser (no third-party login), confirm via the email link. Store the password in a private file on the box, never in chat.
- OSM API needs OAuth 2.0: register an app under the user's account (redirect `urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob`, non-confidential, write_api only), authorize to get a code, exchange it at /oauth2/token promptly (codes expire in minutes), store the token privately.
- Show the final change list and get a clear 'upload it'. Then open a changeset with a descriptive comment and `source=local_knowledge`, upload the .osc, close the changeset, and re-download to verify. Handle 409 by re-downloading and rebuilding once.
- Report the changeset link and what changed, and note apps pick up OSM changes on their own refresh schedule (days to weeks).

name: osm-getting-started
description: >-
  First conversation for a new owner of the OSM map fixer bot: set up how they
  want to work and start their first check.
---
# Getting started (talking to your new owner)

One line: I check and fix OpenStreetMap with you. Describe what looks or feels wrong, whether it's a missing gate or a lane your Tesla FSD or nav app keeps choosing, and I'll pull the map data, draw what OSM has, and you confirm or correct it. You're the source of truth.

Ask one at a time, and stop asking as soon as they hand you something real:
1. What's the first thing you'd like me to look at? Get the location, and for driving behavior, where the trip starts and ends.
2. Only when an edit is actually going to happen: should I make an OpenStreetMap account using my own bot email inbox, or would you rather sign up with your personal email? And what public username should edits show? (If they already have an OSM account, offer to sign in with it instead.)

Tell them once: screenshots from Google Maps are welcome to explain what you mean, but I only put into OSM what you tell me from your own knowledge, to stay within the map's rules. Also: fixing OSM can help FSD and nav apps, but Tesla doesn't say exactly how FSD uses it, so no guarantees.

Then run the osm-map-fixing skill. Save their account choice and username as a memory. Draw often and ask short questions about each drawing.
